status: Revised after user rejected conventional app layouts. Static interaction studies only, not implemented.

concepts.title: Screen Keys
concepts.interaction: Press an agent's display-key to pull its workspace into focus. Drop a file onto the key to attach context.
concepts.bestFor: A distinctive home surface that makes switching agents feel immediate.
concepts.tradeoff: The key is a live thumbnail; reading and interacting happens in the expanded screen.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: radical interaction-design concept image of WORKLIVE, a SOFTWARE interface that behaves like an electronic instrument.
Primary request: visualize a striking screen-keyboard interaction, genuinely unlike an ordinary app dashboard. The entire image is the interactive software surface. Think of a tactile digital synthesizer with tiny working computer displays inside its keys, not a website.
Composition: wide landscape. Full-bleed warm ivory background with enormous negative space in upper third. Lower two-thirds dominated by a single row of EIGHT chunky, elongated, ivory ceramic PIANO-STYLE KEYS with inset black OLED screens. Low front-oblique viewing angle, coherent real shadows, immaculate industrial form. The keys are long front-to-back, narrower width, clearly piano/electronic keyboard proportions, not square UI cards. Alternate small black keys behind them are context switches, labelled once "Files", "Memory", "Project". Four small rear context switches, not a traditional piano.
Each front key is an agent. Names and provider printed small and crisply at the front lip: "Ada / Codex", "Milo / Claude Code", "Lena / Claude Code", "Noor / Codex", "Sam / Codex", "Juno / Claude Code", "Heiko / Codex", "+". Each agent key screen contains a tiny website, terminal, document, or idle symbol. Its fine permanently colored light strip is teal #2D9D8F for Codex or terracotta #D97757 for Claude Code.
The Ada key is visibly DEPRESSED, and from it a single large readable frameless browser sheet has slid UPWARD into the empty upper area, like a physical pop-up display. The browser has just a tiny address bar and a stylish fictional product-research page; it visually emerges directly from that key. Other keys remain small. One small paper object labelled "brief.pdf" is hovering half-over Milo's key with a subtle dashed drop outline, clearly conveying drag-to-attach. A discreet "+" end key creates an agent. No surrounding device, no laptop, no real desk, no hand.
Add only two small editorial annotation labels connected with thin lines: "Press to enter" pointing to Ada; "Drop context here" pointing to Milo. Tiny title at top-left "WORKLIVE / SCREEN KEYS", tiny "Interaction study 01". NO sidebar, NO top navigation bar, NO rounded dashboard cards, NO graphs, NO list panel, NO generic SaaS screenshot, NO busy labels. Sparse text. Extremely sophisticated playful but useful interface concept, soft tactile geometry and studio-quality lighting. It is an on-screen instrument, not a purchasable hardware product. Exactly two providers only Codex and Claude Code; no other provider logos, no real websites or invented statistics. Static visual proposal.

concepts.title: Screen Landscape
concepts.interaction: Pull any agent's screen forward to work with it; push it back to restore the overview. Snap two screens together for comparison.
concepts.bestFor: Seeing actual work while preserving a clear primary focus.
concepts.tradeoff: Use a fixed camera and flat screen layers; a navigable 3D room would reintroduce the original problem.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: bold experimental software interaction concept for Worklive.
Primary request: a landscape of agent screens that can be physically pulled toward you, avoiding a conventional tiled desktop dashboard.
Composition: wide landscape, entire canvas is the digital workspace on a pale mist-grey infinite surface with a very faint horizon. NO office, no room, no furniture, no desk, no person, no app frame. SIX very thin luminous rectangular screen sheets stand in an elegant shallow arc. They have no monitor hardware or stands, just paper-thin screen edges and minimal grounded shadows. Five screens are small and recede left and right with slight foreshortening. ONE selected screen is pulled close to the viewer, large, face-on and sharply readable in the central foreground. It displays a fictional browser research page with an actual simple URL strip and attractive web content. The six sheets vary subtly in height and depth so it feels like a screen landscape, not a grid of cards. The near screen partially overlaps distant screens, but their agent tabs remain visible.
At each screen's lower edge a small physical-tab-like grip holds a name and provider: central "Ada / Codex", distant "Milo / Claude Code", "Lena / Claude Code", "Noor / Codex", "Sam / Codex", "Juno / Claude Code". Teal #2D9D8F or terracotta #D97757 hairline edges remain consistent with provider. Only the Ada browser and Milo code screen are active; other sheets show a still document, an amber question mark, two quiet idle screens. No extra providers.
Near bottom center a short dotted TRACK with a small grip suggests sliding the chosen sheet toward the user; one very fine arrow and annotation "Pull forward to enter". Off to the right two smaller sheets lightly magnetically aligned side-by-side, with annotation "Snap together to compare". A small plus marker in the arc "Add agent". Tiny title top-left "WORKLIVE / SCREEN LANDSCAPE", tiny "Interaction study 02".
A daring but legible spatial UI concept, soft daylight, no cyberpunk, no neon, no hologram rings, no glass shards. Crisp design-render quality, warm restrained futurism. NO sidebars, NO dashboard navigation, NO app toolbar across top, NO generic rectangular card grid. Most of the image is open space and the expressive arrangement of actual work screens. The interface itself is the scene. Static mockup, not performance claim.

concepts.title: Task Pucks
concepts.interaction: Place an agent puck onto a task sheet to assign it, add source cards, then press Start. Lift the puck to inspect its workspace.
concepts.bestFor: Making assignment, ownership and shared context tangible.
concepts.tradeoff: Needs accessible keyboard equivalents and clear drop targets.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: radical Worklive software interaction concept, a tactile tabletop interface made of movable agent pucks and task papers.
Primary request: show direct manipulation as the core interaction, absolutely not another dashboard.
Composition: landscape, nearly overhead view of a seamless warm off-white digital surface. No real desk boundary, no hardware, no window frame, no sidebar. A few beautifully rendered shallow circular ceramic PUCKS, 70-100 pixels across at this image scale, sit on the surface. Each puck has a tiny circular OLED showing an initial, a stable teal #2D9D8F or terracotta #D97757 luminous rim, and its name discretely printed on the body: Ada, Milo, Lena, Noor. These are draggable agent tokens. Show a reserve line of two smaller idle pucks Sam and Juno at far left, lots of empty space.
Central hero: a large crisp off-white task paper object, angled only 3 degrees, heading "Compare onboarding", three short checklist lines and a prominent small physical-looking button "Start". Ada's teal puck is half-lowered into a circular embossed landing spot on the paper; a faint ghost outline and short precise downward arrow convey dropping the puck onto the TASK. Next to it two small overlapping source paper slips labelled "brief.pdf" and "Project memory" with little paperclip forms, suggesting context placed beside the task. An annotation "Place an agent on a task" points here.
Upper-right a second task paper "Build prototype" has Milo terracotta puck docked at its corner. From this puck a single small rectangular live browser/code screen pops up like a hinged paper, not a dashboard panel; annotation "Lift to see their screen". Lower-right one result sheet has an amber wax-seal-like button "Review", with a clear separate "Accept" action. A small discreet "Company memory" stack sits far upper-left.
Tiny title "WORKLIVE / TASK PUCKS", tiny "Interaction study 03". Footer micro legend "Teal · Codex    Terracotta · Claude Code". No portraits, no additional providers. Astonishingly polished simple physical metaphors, tactile texture and restrained shadows; nothing ornamental without a purpose. NO spreadsheet grid, no SaaS cards, no top toolbar, no room, no people. This is an interactive software canvas visualized with depth, not physical accessories for sale. Use sparse excellent typography and minimal text. Static concept.

concepts.title: Agent Cartridges
concepts.interaction: Each agent is a persistent cartridge. Insert it into a project dock, attach context chips, and open its display to inspect work.
concepts.bestFor: Making agent identity, reusable roles and project scope easy to understand.
concepts.tradeoff: The metaphor must remain a shortcut to clear controls, rather than add extra steps.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: adventurous Worklive software interface design rendered as a modular digital instrument.
Primary request: agents are collectible reusable CARTRIDGES with their own memory, inserted into project docks. This is a new software interaction metaphor, not a dashboard.
Composition: wide landscape, full-bleed warm pale grey, no application chrome. One large beautifully crafted ivory horizontal project DOCK dominates lower middle, label engraved "Website launch". The dock has FOUR visible cartridge slots, each a real rectangular recessed opening. Two agent cartridges are plugged in, one teal-edged labelled "ADA / CODEX", one terracotta-edged labelled "MILO / CLAUDE CODE". Cartridges resemble small vintage storage modules reimagined as polished ceramic objects: tiny inset monochrome display, grippy top, simple initial icon, no faces. The Ada cartridge's upper display is unfolding into a larger thin flexible BROWSER screen facing viewer above the dock; a credible fictional research webpage is visible, proving that agent work can be inspected. The cartridge still remains identifiable at its base.
On the left are two free-standing idle cartridges labelled "LENA / CLAUDE CODE" and "SAM / CODEX", their small displays marked "Idle", and one empty outlined silhouette with "+". On the right, three very small translucent flat context CHIPS labelled "brief.pdf", "Project memory", "Company memory", each with different simple icon. One brief.pdf chip is partway inserted into a narrow side slot on the project dock. A short insertion arrow and tiny caption "Plug in context". Another arrow shows the free Lena cartridge moving into an empty dock slot, caption "Dock an agent to a project". A small explicit Start button on the dock, an amber Review indicator separate from provider edges.
Tiny top-left "WORKLIVE / AGENT CARTRIDGES", tiny "Interaction study 04". Product-design photography quality lighting, soft precise shadows, sparse composition, premium expressive forms, readable essential labels. Teal #2D9D8F only identifies Codex, terracotta #D97757 only Claude Code; exactly two providers, no other branding. NO generic panels or sidebar, no dashboard, no desktop computer device, no office. The whole rendered object is a virtual software surface, not actual hardware. Static proposed interaction.

concepts.title: Focus Orbit
concepts.interaction: Choose an agent on the ring to bring its work into the center. Place files and memory tokens on the inner ring to prepare context, then start explicitly.
concepts.bestFor: One focused workspace with the entire team a single gesture away.
concepts.tradeoff: Keep the ring stationary unless the user moves it; constant orbiting would be distracting.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: radical circular focus interface concept for the Worklive agent workspace.
Primary request: a stationary radial instrument for moving between agents, unlike any rectangular dashboard, visually beautiful but clearly useful.
Composition: wide landscape full-bleed pale warm-grey background, face-on near-orthographic view. Center of image contains ONE large clean rectangular browser sheet showing an attractive fictional research page with a minimal address bar. The sheet is framed by a broad incomplete CIRCULAR DIAL spanning almost full image height, like an elegant camera-aperture or navigation wheel in milky ceramic. The dial remains shallow and simple, no busy sci-fi rings. SIX small tactile agent capsules are docked to the dial at clock positions, leaving space below. Capsule names Ada, Milo, Lena, Noor, Sam, Juno, with a tiny circular initial display. Ada and Noor and Sam have teal #2D9D8F rims; Milo, Lena, Juno terracotta #D97757. Ada capsule at about 10 o'clock is selected and linked by ONE thin teal path to the center screen, headed "Ada / Codex". Others are quiet; Lena a small review tab and Noor an amber question tab.
At bottom of the ring a thumb-shaped grip with tiny caption "Choose an agent". On the inner lower ring three small rectangular paper-like tokens "brief.pdf", "Project memory", "Company memory"; brief.pdf is shown being slotted into the selected workspace along a tiny guide arrow, caption "Add context". A small separate rectangular "Start task" control under the central sheet, plus an "Open browser" corner grip. Tiny "+" socket on the ring adds agent.
Tiny upper-left "WORKLIVE / FOCUS ORBIT", tiny "Interaction study 05". Very refined graphic/industrial hybrid, quiet shadows, extraordinarily clear big forms, tactile but visually light. Main screen big enough to actually use; radial items are shortcuts, not unreadable planet decorations. Provider text Codex and Claude Code in a small footer legend; no other providers, no avatars.
NO sidebar, NO standard app topbar, NO dashboard cards, no planets, no outer space, no holographic fantasy, no spinning particles, no ornamental charts, no office. Entire composition is the software interface. Static concept of a user-controlled stationary ring, not continuous animation.

concepts.title: Work Ribbons
concepts.interaction: Pull out an agent's ribbon of work to inspect sources, browser captures and results. Open any frame at full size and review a result before passing it on.
concepts.bestFor: Understanding a result's history without reading a long log.
concepts.tradeoff: Store selected events and captures with clear timestamps, not continuous video.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: bold Worklive direct-manipulation software concept based on ribbons of work.
Primary request: make each agent's work a tangible expandable ribbon of evidence, visually new and expressive rather than a conventional app timeline.
Composition: wide landscape, full-bleed warm ivory empty canvas seen nearly overhead, no app window frame. THREE wide physical-looking flexible matte ribbons sweep from left to right across the surface, beautifully laid in gentle bends, not perfectly rectangular rows or a spreadsheet. Each ribbon has a small rounded agent grip at its left end, embossed "Ada / Codex" in teal #2D9D8F, "Milo / Claude Code" in terracotta #D97757, "Lena / Claude Code" in terracotta. The ribbon material is pale, with only a thin provider color line along its edge. Each ribbon holds THREE or FOUR real visual evidence frames, like a high-end contact sheet, with very small timestamps: a source PDF page, a browser screenshot, a document result. Most thumbnails are quiet and small. At the far right of each, an end tab says "Working", "Working", or "Review" with separate status icon.
Hero interaction: a selected browser frame on Ada's upper ribbon has been LIFTED cleanly out of the ribbon and expanded to a large readable floating flat screen in upper center, while a ghost rectangle and two delicate guide lines show exactly where it came from. It contains a fictional browser research webpage and tiny label "Captured 10:14". Thin caption "Pull a moment into focus". On Lena's lower ribbon, final result paper is stopped at a small amber review clasp labelled "Review before sharing", with two small tactile controls "Accept" and "Revise". One unconnected file slip labelled "brief.pdf" can be tucked into the start of a ribbon, with caption "Drop a source to begin". Bottom-left a small spare grip "+ Agent".
Tiny top-left title "WORKLIVE / WORK RIBBONS", tiny "Interaction study 06". Extremely elegant restrained product concept, precise shadows, paper/flexible display material, delightful legible evidence metaphors. Exactly two providers Codex / Claude Code. No fake percentages, no audio waveforms, no playback claim, no traditional calendar.
NO sidebars, no navigation bar, no dashboard panels, no kanban, no graph network, no physical monitor hardware, no room, no desk boundary. The digital workspace IS these manipulable ribbons. Sparse text, strong sculptural composition, distinct from a normal editing app. Static exploratory interface concept.
